paragraphs.source_en: Sena-hime’s eyes widened with fury, and she pressed her lips tightly shut. She had been consumed by rage, yet the bitter irony in Ieyasu’s words gradually restored her reason. Was it better to die bravely in battle, or accept the girl from Owari and cling ignobly to life? When a person faced a choice between life and death, marriage was indeed no longer the sole measure of happiness. However unwillingly, Sena-hime had to concede that Ieyasu was right.
